Project.Name: FileCompare
Project.Description: A Blazor Server single-page reconciliation tool that compares a "Converter output file" against a "Client expected file" (both semicolon-delimited, first line = headers). The user selects one or more key columns (composite key, ordered) and a single numeric column to compare. Matching rows are compared on that one numeric column; differences are grouped into configurable magnitude buckets. Results are shown as an expandable tree table grouped by key.
Project.Type: ASP.NET Core Blazor Server (single page, interactive server-side rendering)

TechStack.UIFramework: Blazor Server (single .razor page, no client-side WASM). Custom recursive Razor component for the tree table (no external UI library required; a component library such as Radzen/MudBlazor MAY be used if it speeds up the tree-table but is not required).

OtherLibraries.Library: ClosedXML (MIT) — generates the multi-sheet .xlsx export for F8; no other libraries required beyond built-in Blazor InputFile component and ASP.NET Core

Architecture.Pattern: Layered: Models / Services (parsing, key-matching, comparison, difference-grouping — all plain C#, unit-testable, no Blazor dependency) / single Razor page (Home.razor) with sub-components (FileDropUpload, DualListKeySelector, CompareColumnSelector, GroupingSettings, ResultTreeTable)
Architecture.ProjectStructure: single Blazor Server project: FileCompare.csproj, plus FileCompare.Tests for unit tests of the services

Field.name: Format
Field.notes: chosen input file type; applies to both the Converter and Client files for a given comparison run

Field.name: Delimiter
Field.notes: field delimiter used only when Format = DelimitedText; one of ';' (default), tab, '|'; fixed to ',' when Format = Csv

Field.name: Headers
Field.notes: column names from first line, in file order

Field.name: Rows
Field.notes: each row keyed by header name

Field.name: OrderedKeyColumns
Field.notes: composite key, in the order the user arranged them (up/down)

Field.name: ColumnName
Field.notes: single numeric column selected for comparison

Field.name: Groups
Field.notes: user-defined; each has an absolute-difference upper bound; default is a single group with boundary 0.5

Field.name: KeyValues
Field.notes: values of the ordered key columns for this row

Field.name: OtherColumnValues
Field.notes: non-key, non-compare column values, for display context; rendered as a single combined column whose header is the joined column names and whose value is the joined values, both separated by '; ', with no 'ColumnName:' prefix on the values

Field.name: ConverterCompareValue
Field.notes: value of the compare column from the Converter file, null if row absent there

Field.name: ClientCompareValue
Field.notes: value of the compare column from the Client file, null if row absent there

Field.name: Status
Field.notes: Added = key exists only in Converter file; Deleted = key exists only in Client file

Field.name: DifferenceGroup
Field.notes: set only when Status = Different; which configured bucket the AbsoluteDifference falls into

Field.name: Rows
Field.notes: all rows with their computed status

Feature.Title: File upload: browse and drag & drop
Feature.Description: Two upload zones on the page, each supporting both a file-browse dialog and drag-and-drop, labeled "Converter output file" and "Client expected file".

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Each upload zone shows its label ("Converter output file" / "Client expected file") and accepts a file via click-to-browse or by dragging a file onto the zone.
Visual feedback (e.g. highlight) when a file is dragged over the zone.
After a file is dropped/selected, the zone shows the file name and a way to replace it.
Upload errors (wrong format, unreadable file) shown inline near the relevant zone, not as a crash.

Feature.Title: Parse and validate headers
Feature.Description: Parse both files according to the selected input file type (F9) — delimited text, first line = headers, split on the selected delimiter. The set of column names in both files must match exactly.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Trims whitespace around each header and field value.

If the header sets differ (missing column, extra column, or renamed column, case-sensitive) in either file, comparison is blocked and a clear error is shown listing the mismatched column names — this is a hard failure ("throw"), not a warning.

Header-set comparison treats umlaut case variants consistently — Ä/ä, Ö/ö, and Ü/ü are matched as equivalent pairs (case-insensitive for these letters specifically) even though other ASCII letters remain case-sensitive, so encoding/casing differences in umlauts alone don't produce a false header-mismatch error.

Delimited-text files are read as UTF-8 (with BOM detection) by default, with automatic fallback to Windows-1252/ISO-8859-1 if the content isn't valid UTF-8, so German umlaut characters (ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü, ß) in headers and values are read correctly rather than as mojibake or replacement characters.
Gracefully reports an error if a data row has a different number of fields than the header row.
Handles empty lines by skipping them.

Feature.Title: Key column(s) selection (dual list, ordered)
Feature.Description: Once headers are validated, show all columns in an "Available" list. User moves one or more columns into a "Selected Keys" list to form a composite key, and can move entries up/down within that list to set key precedence order.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Two-list ("dual listbox") UI: Available Columns and Selected Key Columns, with controls to move items between them (e.g. arrows or drag).

Double-clicking a column in the Available Columns list moves it into Selected Key Columns (appended at the end); double-clicking a column in the Selected Key Columns list moves it back to Available Columns. This works as an alternative to the arrow buttons in both lists.
Up/down controls reorder items within the Selected Key Columns list.

If a column named "PersonalNr", "Lohnart", and/or "TextLohnart" is present in the headers, it is automatically pre-populated into Selected Key Columns by default (in that order: PersonalNr, then Lohnart, then TextLohnart).
At least one key column must be selected before the user can proceed to compare-column selection.

Feature.Title: Compare column selection
Feature.Description: User selects exactly one numeric column as "the column to compare". This is the only column whose values are checked for equality between the two files; all other non-key columns are display-only context.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Dropdown/list only offers columns that are not already used as key columns.
Only numeric-type columns are selectable (values must parse as decimal); non-numeric columns are excluded or disabled with an explanation.
If a column named "Betrag" is present and numeric, it is pre-selected by default.
"Compare" action is disabled until a valid compare column is selected.

Feature.Title: Row matching and status computation
Feature.Description: Match rows between the two files using the ordered composite key. Classify each row's status.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Row present in both files (same composite key) with equal compare-column values → Status = Matching.
Row present in both files with differing compare-column values → Status = Different; compute AbsoluteDifference = |ConverterValue - ClientValue|.
Row whose composite key exists only in the Converter file → Status = Added.
Row whose composite key exists only in the Client file → Status = Deleted.
Duplicate composite-key values within a single file are detected and reported as a warning, not a crash.
Uses in-memory dictionary lookups (O(n)) rather than nested-loop comparison, so it scales to large files.

Feature.Title: Difference-magnitude grouping (configurable)
Feature.Description: For rows with Status = Different, group them by how large the AbsoluteDifference is, using user-configurable bucket boundaries (e.g. 0–0.5, 0.5–1, 1–1.5 ...).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Settings panel lets the user specify how many groups to use and the absolute-value boundary for each group.
Buckets are applied as: group 1 = 0 < diff ≤ boundary1, group 2 = boundary1 < diff ≤ boundary2, etc.; a final "greater than last boundary" group catches any remainder.
Changing the grouping settings and re-running updates the Different-entries grouping without needing to re-upload files.
A sensible default is provided if the user doesn't customize it: a single group with boundary 0.5 (i.e. 0 < diff ≤ 0.5, with everything above 0.5 falling into the overflow group).

Feature.Title: Tree-table results view
Feature.Description: Display comparison results as an expandable tree table.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Column headers, left to right: each key column's name (in selected order), then the compare column's name suffixed "(Converter)" in bold, then the compare column's name suffixed "(Client)" in bold, then a single combined column for all remaining "other" (non-key, non-compare) columns. That column's header is the names of those remaining columns joined with "; " (e.g. "Name; Department"), and each row's value is just the corresponding values joined with "; ", in the same order, with no column-name prefix (e.g. "Alice; Sales") — rather than one column per source column.
Top level of the tree has four nodes, each showing its label and row count in parentheses: "Matching entries (N)", "Added entries (N)", "Deleted entries (N)", "Different entries (N)".
Under "Different entries", rows are further grouped by difference-magnitude bucket (from F6), each bucket labeled with its range and count.

Within any node/bucket, rows are grouped hierarchically by key column values in order: expanding shows the first key column's distinct values (with counts); expanding one of those shows the second key column's distinct values within it; and so on until the last key level, which expands to show the actual matched row(s) with all column values.
Expand/collapse is interactive (click to expand/collapse each tree node) without a full page reload.
Tree remains usable for large result sets (e.g. virtualization or lazy expansion rather than rendering everything at once).
Umlaut characters (ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü, ß) in key values, other column values, and column headers render correctly throughout the tree — no mojibake or replacement characters.

Feature.Title: Export results
Feature.Description: Button to download the full comparison result as a multi-sheet Excel (.xlsx) workbook from the browser, split so each status group and each difference-magnitude bucket is its own sheet.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: "Download report" button appears once results are shown and triggers a browser file download of an .xlsx workbook.

Workbook contains a "Summary" sheet with the Matching/Added/Deleted/Different counts, the difference-grouping boundaries used, a row count for each configured difference-magnitude bucket, and any warnings (e.g. duplicate keys).

On the Summary sheet, the Added count is labeled "Added (Rows found only in the Converter output file)" and the Deleted count is labeled "Deleted (Rows found only in the Client expected file)"; this longer wording is for the Summary sheet's labels only — the "Added"/"Deleted" sheet tab names (see below) are unaffected, to stay within Excel's naming constraints.

Workbook contains one sheet each for "Matching", "Added", and "Deleted", listing that group's rows with key values, both compare values, and a single combined column for all other columns (same joined-header/joined-values format as F7, with no column-name prefix) — matching the tree table's column order: keys, then compare values, then the combined column.

Workbook contains one additional sheet per difference-magnitude bucket (from F6), named after that bucket's range (e.g. "Diff 0-0.5", "Diff gt 0.5"), each including an AbsoluteDifference column between the compare values and the combined other-columns column.
Sheet names are sanitized and de-duplicated to satisfy Excel's naming constraints (max 31 characters, no \ / ? * [ ] : characters).
Umlaut characters (ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü, ß) in key values, other column values, and column headers are preserved exactly in the exported workbook, matching what is shown in the tree table.

Feature.Title: Input file type selection (CSV / delimited text)
Feature.Description: Before/alongside the upload zones, the user selects the type of the input files: "CSV" (comma-delimited, .csv) or "Delimited text" (default: semicolon; user-selectable delimiter). This selection applies to both the Converter output file and the Client expected file for a given comparison run — mixed formats between the two files are not supported.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A file-type selector (e.g. radio buttons) offers "CSV" and "Delimited text", defaulting to "Delimited text".
When "CSV" is selected, files are parsed as comma-delimited with no delimiter picker shown; upload zones accept ".csv".
When "Delimited text" is selected, a delimiter dropdown appears offering Semicolon (default), Tab, and Pipe (Comma is covered by the dedicated CSV option, not duplicated here).
Both the Converter output file and the Client expected file are parsed using the same selected format and delimiter; there is no per-file override.
Changing the file type or delimiter after both files are already uploaded automatically re-parses both files and re-runs header validation (F2), without a full page reload.
If an uploaded file cannot be parsed as the selected type (e.g. no occurrences of the selected delimiter found), a clear inline error is shown near the relevant upload zone instead of a crash.

Screen.name: Home (single page)
Screen.Purpose: The entire workflow happens on one page: upload both files, choose keys and compare column, configure grouping, compare, and explore results as a tree — all without navigating away.

Elements.Element: File-type selector: "CSV" or "Delimited text" (with delimiter dropdown: Semicolon/Tab/Pipe) (F9)
Two upload zones with browse + drag-and-drop: "Converter output file", "Client expected file"
Header-mismatch error banner (shown only if validation in F2 fails)
Dual-list key column selector with up/down reorder (F3)
Compare column dropdown, numeric columns only (F4)
Difference-grouping settings panel: number of groups + boundary value per group (F6)
Tree-table results area (F7): top-level Matching/Added/Deleted/Different nodes with counts, expandable down through key levels to individual rows
"Download report" button (nice-to-have) — downloads a multi-sheet .xlsx workbook (F8)

NonFunctional.Performance: Should comfortably handle files with tens of thousands of rows using in-memory dictionary lookups for key matching (O(n), not O(n^2)). Parsing/comparison should run off the Blazor Server UI thread for large files so the page stays responsive. Tree rendering should not force-render the entire result set at once (lazy/virtualized expansion).
NonFunctional.ErrorHandling: Header mismatches, malformed rows, unreadable uploads (including files that don't match the selected input type per F9), non-numeric values in the compare column, or invalid grouping settings all produce clear, inline UI messages — no unhandled exceptions or stack traces shown to the user.
NonFunctional.Logging: Not required beyond on-page error messages.
NonFunctional.Configuration: Max upload file size configured reasonably (e.g. up to 50MB) via Blazor InputFile settings.
NonFunctional.Encoding: Delimited-text input is read as UTF-8 (BOM-aware) with automatic fallback to Windows-1252/ISO-8859-1, so German umlaut characters (ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü, ß) round-trip correctly end-to-end: from file read, through header validation, key/compare matching, and tree-table display, to the exported Excel workbook. The exported .xlsx (F8) is natively Unicode and needs no special handling on output.

Constraints.Constraint: No database — pure C#/.NET and built-in/optional Blazor UI components.

Supported input file types are CSV (comma, first line = headers) and delimited text (semicolon/tab/pipe, first line = headers) — see F9. Both files in a comparison run must use the same type and delimiter.
Single page only — no multi-page navigation/routing needed.
Compare column must be numeric (decimal); non-numeric "value comparison" columns are out of scope for this version.

Deliverable.Output: Runnable .NET 8 Blazor Server solution (.sln + .csproj + source files) with a README explaining how to build and run it (dotnet run), plus sample input files for testing.
